purpose: Prove the registered indexer-selection fusion did what its pair gains said, by profiling the lane before and after it, and re-derive the cost model so the next target is not a stale one.

profiled_forward_ms.note: profiling instrument counts all kernels, so these exceed the 69.99 ms timed step; the comparison between them is what this receipt is for

ai_cpu_operators_per_forward.verdict: 8 of the 9 mask-sort-cast sites are gone, exactly as the fusion claims: Cast, Sort and Greater each fall from 9 to 1, and the surviving 1 of each is site B at attention.py:1326, which was deliberately left on torch because the rank kernel measured 0.66x there. AI_CPU device time falls 1603.3 us and the task count falls 31 to 7.

caveat: COMMUNICATION moved from 19175.5 to 20620.7 us between the two captures with an identical task count of 130.2. That is the MoE routing straggler wait varying run to run, not a regression caused by the fusion, and it is larger than the AI_CPU saving - which is why the pair protocol, not a single profile, is what registers a gain.

next_target.item: The remaining AI_CPU operator is Index, 4 a forward at 898.5 us, and it is no longer the selection itself: tp.gather at attention.py:1193 is a collective all-gather under the banded path, not an AI_CPU index. So the four come from elsewhere in the indexer.
next_target.but: the whole AI_CPU bucket is now 1158.6 us of a 78.6 ms profiled forward, about 1.3% of the real step, so its ceiling is small. The two dominant items are still the scale-LUT cube kernel at 15.4% (already bounded at under 2.4 ms upside) and communication at 26.2% (straggler wait, closed twice over).
next_target.honest_position: the cheap, well-identified items in this lane are now largely spent. Further gains need either a faster compute kernel for the LUT path or a decision on the speculative-decoding constraint.
